message.text: I want to check how the store.Driver interface is defined and how it's wired up in the db package.

q03.

**`postgres.DB` — `store/db/postgres/postgres.go`**

The struct is declared as plain `DB` inside package `postgres`, so it's referred to as `postgres.DB` from outside:

```16:19:store/db/postgres/postgres.go
type DB struct {
	db      *sql.DB
	profile *profile.Profile
}
```

It satisfies the `store.Driver` interface (defined in `store/driver.go`) via pointer receiver methods. The core lifecycle methods (`GetDB`, `Close`, `IsInitialized`, `GetDatabaseSize`) live in `store/db/postgres/postgres.go`, while the rest of the interface is implemented across sibling files in the same package — `memo.go`, `user.go`, `attachment.go`, `idp.go`, `inbox.go`, `reaction.go`, and others.

`postgres.NewDB(profile)` constructs it and returns it as a `store.Driver`, and it gets selected by driver name in `store/db/db.go`:

```23:24:store/db/db.go
	case "postgres":
		driver, err = postgres.NewDB(profile)
```

For comparison, the parallel implementations are `mysql.DB` in `store/db/mysql/mysql.go` and `sqlite.DB` in `store/db/sqlite/sqlite.go` — all three packages name their struct `DB`.
